title: I'm 25 and working in the UK. Should I buy a RM750,000 unit in KL Sentral?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #212 | FIRST WORK ON INCOME, THEN INVEST IN PROPERTY
excerpt: A 25-year-old graduate in the UK has modelled a KL Sentral unit at over RM1,000 per sq ft. Sean suggests five years building his career first, and explains valuations, exit plans and how deals are crafted.

qa.asker: K, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: K, 25, started a job in the UK six months ago, earns about RM9,000 a month after tax and has no debts; he chose not to buy a car so he could invest. After comparing areas he has picked a new 650 sq ft unit in KL Sentral at about RM750,000, over RM1,000 per sq ft after incentives, with a bank valuation 10% to 15% above the price and expected rent of about RM4 per sq ft. He has budgeted to cover the instalment for a year if it stays empty.
qa.question: Is the valuation margin a good sign, is this a good investment, and how can he make it cash-flow positive?
qa.quote: Best deals are crafted, not found.
qa.answer: There's no rush. At 25, Sean would spend the next five years raising his skills and income, then buy with more capital, more options and a clearer idea of where he will live. If he buys now, a higher valuation doesn't mean he has already made money, and cheaper areas may suit an overseas owner better.

reasons.title: A valuation isn't a sale price
reasons.body: If similar units sell for about RM750,000, that is the market price, whatever the bank's valuation. Many new condos in Kuala Lumpur sell at or even below their SPA price once completed, so a profit four years on isn't guaranteed.

reasons.title: Owning from abroad adds risk
reasons.body: Exchange rates can move against him, managing tenants and repairs from 12 hours away is stressful, and his plans may change if he settles in the UK. He needs an exit plan before he buys.

reasons.title: Cheaper areas are easier to carry
reasons.body: Units of about RM300,000 to RM400,000 in places like Subang Jaya and USJ rent for about RM1,400 to RM1,500. A vacant year there costs far less than at KL Sentral.

reasons.title: Good deals are made, not walked into
reasons.body: Sales galleries sell at the full retail price. Cash allows subsale negotiation, bulk purchase deals can be cheaper, and a well-furnished unit stands out: Sean pays RM100 more a month for a nicely done unit among 15 to 18 similar ones.

actions: Invest in your skills and qualifications for the next few years to raise your income.
Decide where you're likely to settle before buying in another country.
Compare each area's median price per square foot, and avoid paying well above it.
If you buy, choose a unit where the rent covers the instalment on a long loan.
Budget to furnish the unit well so it rents quickly against similar units.
qa.caveat: If he is sure he will return to Malaysia and the numbers work, buying young does get him a 35-year loan and a lower instalment. Sean's own strategy accepts a small monthly top-up while the tenant pays down the loan.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #212. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in May 2023. The episode was sponsored by Dreame, an unrelated vacuum cleaner brand.
